answer.question: What should a Castle Rock homeowner confirm before finalizing a turf layout?
answer.answer: Ask the Town and any association which landscape requirements apply to the property and proposed change, particularly for a newer home. Then compare the usable turf area, access, preparation and finishing in the written estimate. Check incentives directly before counting one in the budget.

blocks.h2: Decide what needs turf and what should stay planted.
paras: A lawn near the patio, a dog area by the door or a putting green can each be a defined part of the yard. Mark beds, walking routes and the space you want for other uses before choosing a final footprint.
For a practice green, discuss putting lengths and any chipping area. On a sloped property, include how you will reach and walk around the green in the design conversation.

blocks.h2: Make the ground work visible in the price.
paras: Point out known wet areas, changes in grade and access restrictions. Removal and preparation can differ between an established downtown yard and a new subdivision property; the estimate should explain the proposed work for yours.

Castle Rock’s published ColoradoScape rule for homes permitted and built after January 1, 2023 allows no turf in front and limits turf in back to 500 square feet. The cited homeowner guidance does not settle whether synthetic turf is included in that limit. Obtain the Town’s answer for your property before sizing a lawn or green, then check the applicable community conditions separately.

blocks.h2: Castle Rock limits lawns on new homes.
paras: The Town's ColoradoScape ordinance, No. 2022-025, took effect on 1 January 2023 for new homes and commercial properties. For a home permitted and built after that date the rule is no turf in the front yard and no more than 500 square feet in the back yard, with the details in the Town's Landscape and Irrigation Criteria Manual (Town of Castle Rock). Homes built before 2023 are outside the rule.

The Town's pages do not say whether artificial turf counts toward that 500 square feet, and the answer decides how much of a back yard can be lawn. If your home is newer, ask the Town before the layout is final, and have the answer in writing.

Nearly every Castle Rock subdivision built since 1990 has an HOA. In Macanta the Town preapproves backyard designs before the first installation; in other neighborhoods, ask your HOA for its preapproved ColoradoScape designs. Colorado law also bars HOA design guidelines from prohibiting nonvegetative turf in the back yard of a detached single-family home (SB23-178).

blocks.h2: The rebate pays to take grass out, not to put turf in.
paras: Castle Rock Water is the Town's own utility, and its ColoradoScape renovation rebate pays $3.25 a square foot to replace living lawn on a home, with a 400 square foot minimum and 1,500 square feet per account, plus $1.00 a square foot for surfaces such as concrete or decking. It states plainly that artificial turf does not qualify for any part of the rebate, for homes or businesses (Castle Rock Water).

Watering runs on a schedule. Under the Stage 1 drought rules in effect since 1 September, homes water two days a week by the last digit of the address: 0 to 3 on Tuesdays and Fridays, 4 to 6 on Sundays and Wednesdays, 7 to 9 on Mondays and Thursdays, and only before 8 a.m. or after 8 p.m. (Castle Rock Water).
So the trade here is simple. Turf earns no rebate in Castle Rock, and it takes that part of the yard off the watering schedule for good.

blocks.h2: Clay and heaving bedrock, so the base does the work.
paras: Castle Rock sits at 6,224 feet on the Front Range's expansive clays, bentonite and montmorillonite, which can swell by up to 20% when wet and push with more than 30,000 pounds per square foot (Colorado Geological Survey). Douglas County also has heaving bedrock, which the survey treats as a separate and more complex hazard (Colorado Geological Survey).

On ground like this, drainage is most of the job: no water pooling by the foundation and none pushed down into the clay. We prepare the site and build the base for your soil before the turf goes down, so rain runs off the way it should.

The ground changes across town. Crystal Valley, Escavera and the streets near the butte have real grade changes, while The Meadows sits on flatter pads. The older blocks downtown around Wilcox and Perry have small, deep lots, alleys and mature trees, and that shade matters: shade keeps turf far cooler in summer.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Castle Rock, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Castle Rock, CO. Two local rules shape the job: homes permitted after 1 January 2023 are limited to no turf in the front yard and 500 square feet in back, and Castle Rock Water's lawn-removal rebate excludes artificial turf. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can I put artificial turf in my front yard in Castle Rock?
faq.a: It depends on when your home was permitted. For homes permitted and built after 1 January 2023, the Town's ColoradoScape rule allows no turf in the front yard, and its pages do not say whether that includes artificial turf. Older homes are outside the rule, though your HOA's design rules may still apply. Ask the Town and your HOA before you design (Town of Castle Rock).

faq.q: Does Castle Rock Water give a rebate for artificial turf?
faq.a: No. Its ColoradoScape renovation rebate pays $3.25 a square foot to replace living lawn and $1.00 for surfaces such as concrete or decking, and states that artificial turf does not qualify for any part of it. Rebates of $600 or more count as taxable income (Castle Rock Water).

faq.q: When can I water a lawn in Castle Rock?
faq.a: Under the Stage 1 drought rules, two days a week set by the last digit of your address, and only before 8 a.m. or after 8 p.m. (Castle Rock Water). Artificial turf needs no watering at all.

faq.q: Can my HOA stop me putting turf in my back yard?
faq.a: Not with a flat ban on a detached single-family home: Colorado's SB23-178 bars HOA design guidelines from prohibiting nonvegetative turf in the back yard. Attached homes and condominiums are not covered. In Macanta the Town also preapproves backyard designs before the first installation (SB23-178).
